name: Smart-Ass Shows
description: Dialogue-heavy, rapid-fire wit. Dense joke writing, meta-humor, cultural references as currency.

questions.questionText: On Arrested Development, what is the Bluth family's recurring catchphrase when doing a magic trick?
In Community, what is the name of the fictional college where the show takes place?
On 30 Rock, what is Tracy Jordan's ridiculous film project that Liz helps him with?
options: All of the above are Tracy Jordan films

questions.questionText: In Frasier, what is the name of Frasier Crane's radio show?

source.description: Frasier Fandom Wiki - The Frasier Crane Show

questions.questionText: On Veep, what political office does Selina Meyer hold at the start of the series?
In It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia, what is the name of the bar the gang owns?

source.description: Always Sunny Fandom Wiki - Paddy's Pub

questions.questionText: On Archer, what is the name of the spy agency Sterling Archer works for in the early seasons?
In Community, what phrase does Abed Nadir frequently use to express approval?
On It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia, what does Charlie Kelly's conspiracy-explaining setup involve?
options: A chalkboard full of scrawled connections (Pepe Silvia)

source.description: Always Sunny Fandom Wiki - Pepe Silvia

questions.questionText: In Frasier, what breed of dog is Eddie, Martin Crane's pet?
On Archer, what is Sterling Archer's biggest fear?
In Community, what is the name of the paintball episode that parodies action movies and became a fan-favorite?
What radio station does Frasier Crane host his show on in Frasier?
questions.funFact: Kelsey Grammer played Frasier Crane for 20 consecutive years across Cheers, Frasier, and the 2023 revival.

questions.questionText: What is the name of Frasier's brother on Frasier?
questions.funFact: David Hyde Pierce was cast as Niles partly because he bore a striking physical resemblance to Kelsey Grammer.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the coffee shop Frasier and Niles frequent?
questions.funFact: Frasier won 37 Primetime Emmy Awards — a record for scripted series at the time.

questions.questionText: What was Martin Crane's profession before retirement on Frasier?
questions.funFact: John Mahoney (Martin) was actually British-born. His American accent on the show was the performance, not the other way around.

questions.questionText: Who narrates Arrested Development?
questions.funFact: Ron Howard also served as executive producer. He occasionally appears on screen as himself in later seasons.

questions.questionText: What does G.O.B. stand for in Arrested Development?
questions.funFact: Will Arnett based G.O.B.'s failed magic acts on real amateur magicians he'd observed at children's birthday parties.

questions.questionText: What condition does Tobias Funke suffer from in Arrested Development?
questions.funFact: A never-nude always wears cutoff jean shorts under their clothes. David Cross wore them in every scene, even ones where they weren't visible.

questions.questionText: What recurring catchphrase do multiple Bluth family members say in Arrested Development?
questions.funFact: The phrase was first said by G.O.B. but eventually almost every Bluth family member says it — a deliberate running gag about hereditary poor judgment.

questions.questionText: What political office does Selina Meyer hold at the start of Veep?
questions.funFact: Julia Louis-Dreyfus won 6 consecutive Emmy Awards for Veep — the most ever by a single performer for the same role.

questions.questionText: What is Gary Walsh's role to Selina Meyer on Veep?
questions.funFact: Tony Hale won 2 Emmys for playing Gary. He also played Buster Bluth on Arrested Development — two iconic sycophantic sidekicks.

questions.questionText: Who created Veep?
questions.funFact: Iannucci previously created The Thick of It, a similar British political satire. Veep was his American reimagining of the concept.

questions.questionText: What sketch show does Liz Lemon run on 30 Rock?
questions.funFact: 30 Rock was based on Tina Fey's real experience as head writer of Saturday Night Live. The original show name was 'The Girlie Show' before Tracy joined.

questions.questionText: What is Kenneth Parcell's job at NBC on 30 Rock?
questions.funFact: The show repeatedly hints that Kenneth may be immortal. In the finale, he's still a page decades later while everyone else has aged.

questions.questionText: Who plays the NBC executive Jack Donaghy on 30 Rock?
questions.funFact: The role was written specifically for Baldwin. He won two Emmys and was nominated every single season the show aired.

questions.questionText: What is Archer's most frequently used catchphrase?
questions.funFact: 'Danger zone!' references the Kenny Loggins song. Archer uses it specifically to annoy Lana, which makes it funnier each time.

questions.questionText: Who voices Sterling Archer?
questions.funFact: H. Jon Benjamin also voices Bob Belcher on Bob's Burgers. There's even a crossover episode where Archer wakes up as Bob.

questions.questionText: What was the original name of Archer's spy agency before it was changed?
questions.funFact: The name ISIS (International Secret Intelligence Service) was dropped due to real-world associations with the jihadist group.

questions.questionText: What fictional Connecticut town is Gilmore Girls set in?
questions.funFact: Stars Hollow was inspired by the real town of Washington Depot, Connecticut, which Amy Sherman-Palladino visited and fell in love with.

questions.questionText: What is the name of Luke's establishment in Gilmore Girls?
questions.funFact: Luke Danes was originally written as a female character named Daisy. The switch to a male love interest happened during rewrites.

questions.questionText: What Ivy League university does Rory Gilmore attend?
questions.funFact: Rory originally wanted Harvard, but Amy Sherman-Palladino chose Yale because it was closer to Connecticut and easier to write into the story.

questions.questionText: Which actress from Gilmore Girls later became a major movie star as Sookie St. James?
questions.funFact: Melissa McCarthy was a relative unknown during Gilmore Girls. Her Oscar-nominated role in Bridesmaids came 7 years after the show premiered.

questions.questionText: What is the major Season 1 twist in The Good Place?
options: The neighborhood is actually the Bad Place
questions.funFact: The twist was so closely guarded that most of the cast didn't know until they read the finale script for Season 1.

questions.questionText: What replaces profanity in The Good Place's censored afterlife?
questions.funFact: The fake swearing was Michael Schur's way of getting around network TV language rules while making the censorship itself a joke.

questions.questionText: What does Janet always clarify she is not on The Good Place?
options: Not a robot and not a girl
questions.funFact: D'Arcy Carden played every version of Janet — Good Janet, Bad Janet, Neutral Janet, and even Disco Janet.

questions.questionText: What is Alexis Rose's signature catchphrase on Schitt's Creek?
questions.funFact: Annie Murphy almost quit acting before being cast as Alexis. She was down to her last $3 when she got the call.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the store David Rose opens in Schitt's Creek?
questions.funFact: Rose Apothecary was inspired by Brooklyn artisanal shops. Dan Levy wanted David's growth to be reflected in building something from nothing.

questions.questionText: What unprecedented feat did Schitt's Creek accomplish at the 72nd Emmy Awards?
options: Won Best Comedy for all 6 seasons
Won more Emmys than any comedy in history
questions.funFact: Schitt's Creek won all seven major comedy Emmy Awards that night — a sweep never accomplished before or since.

questions.questionText: What is Moira Rose's beloved collection that she calls her 'bébés' on Schitt's Creek?
questions.funFact: Catherine O'Hara wore over 100 different wigs throughout the series. Each one had its own name and she helped select them all.

questions.questionText: What hidden object appears in every episode of Psych as an Easter egg?
questions.funFact: The pineapple Easter egg became so beloved that fans created online guides tracking its location in every single episode.

questions.questionText: What does Shawn Spencer do every time he introduces Gus on Psych?
options: Gives him a different fake name
questions.funFact: Gus's fake names include Ovaltine Jenkins, Lavender Gooms, Gus T.T. Showbiz, and Methuselah Honeysuckle — over 170 across the series.

questions.questionText: What is Shawn's go-to response when someone corrects his pronunciation on Psych?
questions.funFact: Dulé Hill's standard response as Gus — 'No, you haven't' — was often improvised and became just as iconic as Shawn's line.

questions.questionText: During what historical period is Derry Girls set?
questions.funFact: Creator Lisa McGee based the show on her own experiences growing up in Derry during The Troubles. Most storylines are semi-autobiographical.

questions.questionText: Why is James Maguire sent to the girls' school in Derry Girls?
options: He's English and the boys' school would kill him
He was expelled from the boys' school
questions.funFact: James being English in a Northern Irish Catholic school during The Troubles is played for laughs, but it's rooted in real sectarian tensions.

questions.questionText: Who is the acid-tongued headmistress at the school in Derry Girls?
questions.funFact: Sister Michael became a breakout character. Siobhán McSweeney said she based her deadpan delivery on nuns she actually knew growing up.

questions.questionText: What is Wayne's signature opening catchphrase on Letterkenny?
options: That's what I appreciates about you
questions.funFact: The show's rapid-fire slang comes from creator Jared Keeso's real experience playing competitive hockey in small-town Ontario.

questions.questionText: What are the three main social groups in the town of Letterkenny?
questions.funFact: The Hicks vs. Skids vs. Hockey Players dynamic mirrors real small-town Canadian social hierarchies that Keeso grew up with.

questions.questionText: What is the population of Letterkenny according to the show's opening?
questions.funFact: The opening — 'There are 5,000 people in Letterkenny. These are their problems.' — parodies the serious tone of Law & Order's opening.

questions.questionText: What spin-off show features the hockey player character Shoresy from Letterkenny?
questions.funFact: Shoresy was only ever heard, never seen, in Letterkenny — always just his voice from a locker room. Jared Keeso plays both Wayne and Shoresy.
